items.headline: No 7:30am CT US release today — next prints are ISM services 9:00am CT (fcst 54.8) and EIA crude 9:30am CT; BoE decides Thu 6:00am CT (hike ~96.7% to 4.00%).

Dollar steadies in the Europe morning after the Asia slide: DXY ~101.39, EUR/USD ~1.1251 (+0.6% vs NY close), GBP/USD ~1.3485 (+0.5%), USD/JPY back to ~158.43 from the 157.63 Asia low, USD/CHF ~0.8169; US 10Y ~4.93% — equities turned higher in Europe after the Asia selloff.
items.source: Reuters Europe morning Nov 4 via Devdiscourse — https://www.devdiscourse.com/article/international/4001570-forex-dollar-slips-as-democratic-victories-in-us-midterms-stoke-ai-jitters

items.headline: Eurozone inflation hits a three-year high: flash CPI 4.0% in October (from 3.8%, in line with the Reuters poll), core steady at 2.5%; services 3.3% (from 3.2%), energy 20.8% y/y — firms December ECB hike bets.
Gold reclaims $4,000: XAU/USD ~$4,041 as the midterm sweep sets up divided government; traders price a December Fed hike at ~82% (CME FedWatch).

Oil rebounds in the Europe morning: Brent ~$104.36 (+0.7%), WTI ~$96.72 (+0.7%) at 0730 GMT, reversing early declines, as traders weigh US-Iran war/diplomacy uncertainty after the midterm sweep; EIA official data due 9:30am CT.
FXStreet early Wednesday: NZD/USD gathers momentum above 0.5600 (+~0.4% on the day) after the jobs miss; AUD/USD climbs back toward 0.7000 as equities rebound; USD/CAD ~1.396.
BoE Thu 6:00am CT: hike to 4.00% priced ~90-97% (Morningstar 96.7%); BBH expects a 7-2 vote — the vote split and the Monetary Policy Report, not the 25bp, are the event for sterling.

Democrats sweep the midterms: AP calls the Senate (flips in NC, SC, OH, TX, KS, IA; Turek's Iowa win sealed it) and NBC/CBS project a House majority — divided government into 2027; dollar slides in Asia on the result.
items.source: AP: Democrats take the Senate; NBC/CBS project the House — midterm sweep ends unified GOP control — https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/elections/2026/11/03/midterm-elections-results-updates-2026--live/91892413007/

items.headline: Dollar slides to a one-month low in Asia: DXY ~101.4 (-0.3%), EUR/USD ~$1.1249 (+0.5%), USD/JPY ~157.63 (+0.7% for the yen) as midterm results land.
Sterling rallies beyond mid-1.3400s in Asia to a fresh high since Sep 16 (GBP/USD ~1.3469) as the dollar slumps on election results; 200-day SMA at 1.3424 broken.
Nikkei falls 3.6% to 60,835 (lowest since early May) as AI shares slide on midterm results; Nasdaq futures -1.8%, S&P futures -0.8%; US futures, yields and Asian AI stocks all lower.
Oil slips in Asia: Brent ~$103.34 (-0.25%), WTI ~$95.56 (-0.55%) as markets weigh midterm results and stalled US-Iran talks; EIA crude data due 9:30am CT today.
BoE preview: derivatives imply a 96.7% chance of a hike to 4.00% on Thu Nov 5 (6:00am CT) — the first rise since Aug 2023 — with three to four more hikes priced through 2027.
ING expects a 7-2 BoE vote to hike to 4.00% Thursday, with a February follow-up more likely than not as headline CPI heads above 4% early next year.
Today's slate: euro-area flash inflation (fcst 4.0%) at 4:00am CT and US ISM services (fcst 54.8) at 9:00am CT; tentative midterm results due through the day.
PBoC sets USD/CNY mid-point at 6.7180 (vs 6.6811 estimate); Carney says US trade talks to intensify as Washington asks less and offers more; WGC: central-bank gold buying jumped 42% in Q3.
NZ jobs MISS: employment -0.1% q/q (vs +0.4% fcst) and unemployment 5.7% (vs 5.5% fcst) in Q3 — NZD/USD fell to 0.5586, lowest close in eleven sessions; RBNZ Dec 9 hike case weakened.
items.source: Stats NZ Q3 labour market release (calendar actuals)

items.headline: API crude stocks draw 5.267M barrels — much bigger than the small expected draw; EIA official data due today 9:30am CT.

Dollar firms into the NY close — DXY ~101.86 (+0.1%), EUR/USD ~1.1184, GBP/USD ~1.3417, USD/JPY ~158.46 (+0.34%) as the JOLTS beat (7.523M) + factory orders beat (+1.8%) lift Dec Fed hike pricing to ~79%
JOLTS BEATS: September openings 7.523M (vs 7.11M fcst, Aug revised to 7.19M); openings rate 4.5%, hires 5.402M, layoffs 1.641M (lowest since Mar 2025) — 10Y touched 4.97% after the release
Factory orders BEAT: September +1.8% m/m (vs +1.2% fcst, prev +0.3%); durable goods +1.9%, nondefense cap goods ex-aircraft +0.6% — second firm US print at 9:00am CT

Macklem restates the BoC line: 'further rate hikes may be needed' but proceed carefully, meeting by meeting; CPI seen ~3.5% by year-end, at/above 3% through much of 2027; Dec hike ~56% — USD/CAD ~1.3993, little changed as oil swings overshadowed the tone

Oil round-trips: Brent's London bounce to $106.61 / WTI $98.06 faded intraday to ~$104.7 / ~$96.6 on unconfirmed US-Iran deal speculation; Iran denied being close to a deal, no agreement announced — gold ~$3,955, second straight gain off Friday's $3,870 low
